source: Hellwig, Zuidema, Stevenson & Lewis (2026) Transformer See, Transformer Do: Copying as an Intermediate Step in Learning Analogical Reasoning (COLM 2026)
finding: Permuted-alphabet letter-string analogies were run on 2025-26 frontier models (GPT 5.2, GPT 4.1, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5 Flash, GPT OSS 120B, Llama 70B and 17B). The paper says a small trained 3-layer model is on par with them. Per-model accuracies are only in figures, not in text. Frontier models still struggle on some transformations that are easy for humans.
numbers: Small MLC model: seen alphabets / new alphabets 96.7 / 93.9 with copy tasks and 200 training alphabets; 60.9 / 26.5 with 20 alphabets and no copy tasks; new transformations stay near 3 to 13 percent. Multi-shot LLM test: Gemini 2.5 Flash and Llama 3.3 70B improved with 1-5 examples; GPT OSS models got worse with 2 or more examples.
quote: many frontier models struggle with transformations that are easy for humans
limits: Frontier numbers are in Figures 2, 14, 15 only; text gives no per-model scores, so gap 2 is not answered with numbers. Greedy decoding on the small model; frontier prompts not read in detail.
agent_relevance: Reasoning-era models are still not clean on mutated letter strings, but the exact gap is unmeasured here. Copy-style exemplars (restating the source before transfer) helped the small model; this supports keeping the source verbatim next to the target.

source: Camposampiero, Hersche, Wattenhofer, Sebastian & Rahimi (2025) Can Large Reasoning Models do Analogical Reasoning under Perceptual Uncertainty?
finding: o3-mini and DeepSeek R1 solve Raven-style matrices well in the clean version but collapse to near chance when the input is longer, has wider value ranges and has noisy attributes. Extra reasoning tokens do not rescue them.
numbers: I-RAVEN to I-RAVEN-X with uncertainty: o3-mini 86.6 to 17.0 percent with 3.4x more reasoning tokens; R1 80.6 to 23.2. Chance 12.5. o3-mini high effort (up to 100k reasoning tokens) only reached 31.0 percent at 53,596 average reasoning tokens. Neuro-symbolic ARLC went 98.6 to 88.0.
quote: sharp decline in OpenAI's o3-mini task accuracy, dropping from 86.6% ... to just 17.0%
limits: Matrix analogy with symbolic attributes, not far-domain verbal analogy or ARN. Early 2025 models (o3-mini, R1). Not a source-to-target conjecture task.
agent_relevance: Reasoning models do not close the transfer gap when the mapping has distractor attributes; a symbolic checker beat them by a wide margin, which supports a code-side check in O7.

source: Ma et al. (2026) A2RBench: An Automatic Paradigm for Formally Verifiable Abstract Reasoning Benchmark Generation
finding: Rule-induction tasks whose answers are verified by code (cycle consistency) are hard for 2025-26 frontier models. The top model stays far below humans; remapping symbols costs accuracy.
numbers: 1,054 tasks from 20 ARC seed rules. Top models 39.8 percent vs humans 68.5 percent on a representative subset. The table lists Gemini3-Pro, GPT-5, GPT-5-Mini, o4-mini, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, GPT-5.2 and others; symbol-remapping gaps are small for the top rows (about 4.6 points in the one row read cleanly). Row-to-model alignment in the extracted table was garbled, so per-model scores are not used.
limits: Abstract rule induction, not analogy between domains. LLM-generated tasks; human subset small and described briefly. Table columns misaligned in text extraction.
agent_relevance: Even GPT-5-class models stay far below humans on fresh rule transfer, so the gap in K09 and K11 has not closed on this kind of item. Verifying generated tasks by an inverse program is a ready pattern for our checker.

source: Fesser, Ektefaie, Fang, Kakade & Zitnik (2026) Evaluating Relational Reasoning in LLMs with REL (ICML 2026)
finding: Accuracy falls with relational complexity (how many entities must be bound at once), not with input size. Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro Preview and GPT-5.2 all show it. More thinking tokens and one-shot examples change little.
numbers: RC 1 and 2 matrix tasks: up to 91 percent even at 30x30. When RC grows with input size (REL-A3, 30x30): Claude and Gemini fall to about 12 percent (chance 12.5), GPT-5.2 drops about 40 percent. REL-A4: only GPT-5.2 above chance (21 percent at 9x9). Token cap 4,096 to 16,384: +2 to 3 points on REL-A4/A5; average change 0.4 percent on REL-C. One-shot ICL on REL-C: +6.6, +3.4, +6.0 points (C1 77.0, C2 43.3, C3 32.7) but the RC trend stays.
quote: performance degrades consistently and monotonically as RC increases
limits: Algebra, chemistry, biology tasks, not analogy transfer. Three models; one-shot ICL on 10 percent of REL-C only.
agent_relevance: A mapping with many jointly bound relations is where an LLM-only O7 will fail even with a large token budget; keep relations few per check and externalise the binding.

source: Fesser et al. (2026) REL, tool-use ablation (Table A.6, REL-C3 isomer completion)
finding: Giving a model a chemistry toolkit (RDKit) did not remove the fall with relational complexity. This is the nearest test of 'counting versus structure': here the failure is not just counting.
numbers: GPT-5.4 with RDKit, recall by observed-molecule count under 20 / 20-40 / over 40: 0.109 / 0.094 / 0.079; precision 0.638 / 0.428 / 0.470. Without tools: Claude Opus 4.5 recall 0.341 / 0.313 / 0.253; Gemini 3 Pro 0.417 / 0.362 / 0.259; GPT-5.2 0.142 / 0.140 / 0.102. 300 to 400 questions per bin.
limits: Different model with tools (GPT-5.4) than without (GPT-5.2), so not a paired ablation; one task family; not letter strings.
agent_relevance: Weak support that code access does not cure structure-binding failures. Gap 7 stays open: no paired with/without-code test on mutated analogy families exists.

source: Sinha, Goel, Kumaraguru, Geiping, Bethge & Prabhu (2025) Can Language Models Falsify? Evaluating Algorithmic Reasoning with Counterexample Creation (REFUTE)
finding: Models are bad at the check step 'find an input that breaks this claim', even when they can solve the problem. This is a direct measure of a counterexample-search verifier for code claims.
numbers: Best agent, o3-mini (high) with code execution feedback, finds a valid counterexample for under 9 percent of incorrect solutions, though its rating implies it solves up to 48 percent of the problems from scratch. Random-search prompting: o3-mini 8.3 percent; with the correct solution supplied (oracle) DeepSeek V3 15.1, R1 9.9. Supplying the correct solution did not close the gap. In RandSearch, 35 percent of samples end with an incorrect counterexample; 86 percent of those from wrong brute-force code, 14 percent from test-case validation errors. Execution feedback removed all validation failures for R1 and V3 (45 and 36 failures at zero shot).
quote: can create counterexamples for only < 9% of incorrect solutions
limits: Competitive-programming claims, where a counterexample is a concrete input. Does not test transferred analogical conjectures. Several table cells garbled in extraction; headline and RandSearch figures taken from text.
agent_relevance: A pure-LLM counterexample search is a weak O7 verifier. A checker that runs code against a ground-truth validator works much better than model-written brute force. Argues for tests that are code-executable, not asked-for-in-prose.

source: Singhi, Bansal, Hosseini, Grover, Chang, Rohrbach & Rohrbach (2025) When To Solve, When To Verify: Compute-Optimal Problem Solving and Generative Verification for LLM Reasoning (COLM 2025)
finding: At equal inference compute, spending on more sampled solutions plus majority vote (self-consistency) beat spending on generative verification of fewer solutions for most budgets. Verification only pays at large budgets.
numbers: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, MATH, 128 problems: GenRM-FT (32 verifications) matches SC with 4x fewer solutions at a fixed solution count, but at equal total compute GenRM first matches SC after up to 8x compute and beats it by +3.8 percent at 128x compute. Also tested Qwen-2.5-7B, Llama-3.3-70B, AIME24, GPQA-Diamond, QwQ-32B (AIME25).
quote: GenRM first matches SC after consuming up to 8x the inference compute
limits: Math answers with a majority vote; verification there is a model reading a solution, not code or counterexample search. Not conjecture transfer.
agent_relevance: Closest equal-token answer to gap 1: a model-judged verification step costs more than extra samples. The O7 claim must be tested with code-based checks, which are cheap.

source: Dip, Zhou & Zhang (2026) Think Again or Think Longer? Selective Verification for Budget-Aware Reasoning (SEVRA)
finding: A gate that verifies only some answers lowered harmful answer flips and tokens vs always verifying, but a simply longer first attempt matched it with fewer tokens. Always-on verification hurt on CommonsenseQA.
numbers: Frozen Qwen3-4B. MATH500: selective 76.3 percent vs always-verify 75.5; post-generation tokens down 26.8 percent; harmful flips 2.2 to 1.0 percent. An 8,192-token initial solve reached 76.0 with 28 percent fewer total tokens. GSM8K: verifies 3.0 percent of items, 93.4 to 94.5, verification tokens down 91.2 percent vs always. CommonsenseQA: always-on verification hurts; SC@5 helps at about 5x token cost.
quote: selective verification is useful, but not a universal compute optimizer
limits: One 4B solver; math and commonsense QA; same-model verification. Not analogical conjectures.
agent_relevance: Verification can undo right answers (harmful flips). If O7 revises a kept conjecture, count flips from right to wrong as well as fixes.

source: Phalod (2026) When Should a Language Model Trust Itself? Same-Model Self-Verification as a Conditional Confidence Signal
finding: Asking a model to audit its own answer gives a confidence signal that depends on task, model and prompt. It beats a likelihood baseline on ARC-Challenge for some models but is unreliable on TruthfulQA-MC, and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B got worse than the baseline.
numbers: No single headline figure; qualitative results across Phi-2, Qwen models and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B, scored by AURC. Only abstract and introduction were read.
limits: Read in part (abstract, intro). Multiple choice QA; small open models.
agent_relevance: Same-model self-check is not a general-purpose error detector. O7 should include at least one check that does not rely on the model's own judgement.

source: Qin, Xia, Wang, Jiao, Hu, Ding, Chen & Joty (2025, v3) Relevant or Random: Can LLMs Truly Perform Analogical Reasoning?
finding: The Yasunaga-style gain does not come from relevance of the self-generated example. Random self-generated examples did as well or better on math; the accuracy of the generated example is the key factor. Tested on GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o-mini, with extra checks on small Llama and Qwen models.
numbers: GPT-3.5, GSM8K / MATH / average: relevant 71.5 / 33.3 / 52.4; no-example (N/A) 75.5 / 36.1 / 55.8; random same-type 75.1 / 36.3 / 55.7; random different 76.3 / 34.1 / 55.2; random biology 75.3 / 34.6 / 54.9. BBH average relevant 63.2 (best); random-same 61.9; random-biology 60.4. GPT-4o-mini GSM8K: relevant 90.7; N/A 91.9; random 92.6 / 92.3 / 93.2; their ICLmath 94.2, ICLbio 94.5. CSQA relevant 70.8 vs N/A 73.4; MBPP 58.2 vs 59.8. Cosine relevance to query: relevant 0.48, oracle 0.64.
quote: self-generated random examples can surprisingly achieve comparable or even better performance
limits: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o-mini plus small Llama and Qwen; no 2025 reasoning model. Order of the N/A row in the extracted BBH table is ambiguous. Their own methods spend extra calls.
agent_relevance: Answers part of gap 3: for non-reasoning models, analogical prompting is no better than prompting with any correct example, and worse than no example on math. Do not claim gains from the analogy itself; test with correct-but-irrelevant sources as a control.

source: Shen, Druckmann & Zou (2026) Unlocking LLM Creativity in Science through Analogical Reasoning
finding: Generating a cross-domain analogy first, then solving, gives far more diverse and novel solutions than same-call-count baselines with Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5.2 and Gemini 3 Flash. Validity of transferred content is judged by an LLM and by downstream implementation on four biomedical tasks.
numbers: 50 research problems, 150 generations per problem. Calls per generation: AR 2, cross-domain baseline 2, no-domain baseline 1. Solution Vendi diversity +90 to 173 percent; binary novelty AR 50.4 / 58.8 / 68.8 percent vs cross-domain 21.6 / 27.2 / 37.9 and no-domain 1.6 / 8.8 / 8.6 (Claude / GPT / Gemini). Humans pick AR as more novel 78 percent of the time (kappa 0.445). Structural depth of analogies was similar across settings (7.06 to 8.60).
limits: Measures novelty and diversity, not correctness of conjectures. Equal calls vs the cross-domain baseline but token counts not compared. LLM-judged metrics.
agent_relevance: A 2026 result that a staged 'analogy then transfer' step helps at equal call count for ideation, which is not what O7 does. Analogy gives breadth; correctness still needs a separate check.

source: Zhang & Zhu (2026) Enhancing Agent Safety Judgment: Controlled Benchmark Rewriting and Analogical Reasoning for Deceptive OOD Scenarios (ROME and ARISE)
finding: Retrieving 3 labelled analogous trajectories and putting them in the prompt raised F1 on deceptive safety cases for all 6 models. Flipping the labels of the retrieved cases cut the gain for 5 of 6, so source correctness matters. For Claude 3.7 Sonnet the flipped condition was higher than standard.
numbers: Average F1 over seed plus 3 challenge sets, zero-shot / ARISE / flipped-labels: GPT-4o 43.27 / 75.37 / 59.17; DeepSeek-V3 46.07 / 81.82 / 70.49; DeepSeek-R1 70.23 / 87.56 / 73.73; Qwen3-8B 50.48 / 65.81 / 46.33; Qwen3-235B 48.75 / 72.50 / 52.87; Claude 3.7 Sonnet 75.36 / 77.04 / 85.33. GPT-4o on the implicit-risk set 31.46 to 67.88; false positive rate on one set 50.0 to 9.0 percent.
limits: Safety classification, not conjecture transfer. Retrieval by embedding similarity; no matched self-generated condition. Temperature 0. Authors call it a task-specific enhancement. The extracted table had one unlabelled row (80.65 ... 88.48) that is not used.
agent_relevance: Retrieved labelled sources help models strongly and wrong labels remove most of the gain, so source quality gates transfer. Partly answers gap 8; self-generated vs retrieved with the same model is still untested.

source: Zhang, Wang et al. (2026) MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
finding: Case memory retrieved by similarity alone plateaus because it cannot filter 'functional distractors'. Re-ranking by a learned utility score from outcomes improves success on agent benchmarks. Selecting sources by outcome is better than by similarity.
numbers: Avg cumulative success +3.8 percent over MemP; +6.2 on ALFWorld and OS tasks, +3.6 on HLE. Held-out transfer: +2.8 percent on average over MemP, ALFWorld +5.8. Q-weight 0 (pure similarity) plateaus; 0.5 best; 1 volatile. Learned Q correlates r = 0.861 with task success, from 21.5 percent in the lowest bin to 88.1 in the highest. On HLE the single-task ablation (0.610) tied MemRL (0.606).
limits: Agent tasks, not analogy; gains small; benchmarks with high within-set similarity benefit most. HLE low similarity (0.186) gave no cross-task gain.
agent_relevance: Supports gap 8: a record of whether a source worked is more useful than similarity. When source similarity is low, nothing transfers.

source: Lee, Song, Yoon, Park & Kang (2026, AAAI) The Curious Case of Analogies: Investigating Analogical Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: Open-weight models (7B to 14B) can encode the relation but often fail to apply it to the new entity. In story analogies with a lexically similar distractor, failures show weak or distractor-biased alignment between source and target tokens.
numbers: Proportional analogies: replacing the first pair with a correct-case pair fixed up to 38.4 percent of wrong cases; patching hidden states at the link fixed up to 38.1 percent more; overall fixes 49.8 (Llama-2-13B), 61.9 (Gemma-7B), 55.3 (Qwen2.5-14B). Story analogies: 360 StoryAnalogy items cut to two options (true target vs noun-similar distractor); correct only if right in both orders; probe accuracy reaches 82.9 percent in middle layers.
limits: Open-weight models only, no reasoning models. Mechanistic study of 2-option items, not generative transfer. Proportional analogies, not conjectures.
agent_relevance: A direct view of the surface-decoy error: when the relation is weakly encoded the distractor wins. Gap 5 is partly answered at the mechanism level; no false-conjecture rate for a relation-level check.

source: Hu, Wang, Shu, Paik, Dong & Zhu (2026) Metaphor-Induced Algorithmic Steering: Cross-Domain Procedural Transfer in LLM Code Generation
finding: A benign, plausible domain-specific skill text written as a metaphor makes code models import a procedure from the source domain (for example brute force instead of dynamic programming) without being asked. The code still runs correctly but is less efficient. A prompt-level detector catches most such skills.
numbers: APPS, per-sample / per-task steering success for metaphorical vs literal skills: Qwen-Coder-Next 80B 23.3 / 41.1 vs 9.6 / 17.8; DeepSeek-Coder-33B 34.5 / 43.8 vs 4.4 / 8.2; Gemma-4-31B 23.6 / 28.6 vs 2.9 / 3.9. Procedure-consistent in 78.4 (Qwen), 21.9 (DeepSeek), 90.9 (Gemma) percent of success cases. Detector macro F1 86.6 percent over 270 examples, recall 100 percent on metaphorical skills.
limits: Skills were searched adversarially by an iterative pipeline, so the rates are upper bounds on natural rates. Efficiency, not truth, is the harmed property. Code-specialised open models.
agent_relevance: Evidence that unrequested analogical transfer occurs in LLMs when a source schema is in context (gap 6). It argues for running O7 whenever a source with a procedure sits in context, not only when an analogy was requested.

source: Shi, Chen, Misra, Scales, Dohan, Chi, Schaerli & Zhou (2023) Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC)
finding: One irrelevant sentence added to a math problem sharply cuts accuracy. Self-consistency recovers much of it. An instruction to ignore irrelevant text also helps.
numbers: Codex and GPT-3.5 (text-davinci-003). Among problems solved without the sentence, no more than 18 percent are solved for all types of irrelevant sentence. Self-consistency with 20 samples: correct answer present in 99.7 percent of problems (96.5 for 0-shot CoT); majority vote +11 points micro accuracy (+35.5 for 0-CoT). Best macro accuracy over prompting methods only 45 percent.
limits: Old models (2022). Arithmetic distractors, not analogical sources. Not run on reasoning models.
agent_relevance: Surface-similar but irrelevant content in context is a standing error source; more samples recover it, and an explicit ignore-instruction helps. A cheap decoy control for O7.

source: Lee & Holyoak (2008) The role of causal models in analogical inference. J Exp Psychol: Learning, Memory, and Cognition 34(5), 1111-1122
finding: Three experiments. Removing a shared preventive cause from the target lowered analogical overlap and similarity but raised judged inductive strength of the effect. Experiment 3 extended this to cross-domain analogy built on higher-order causal relations. Authors conclude analogical inference is mediated by building and running a causal model.
numbers: Abstract only (Europe PMC); no cell values read. Earlier file b11 reports the pattern with GG 89.4 vs GGP 74.4 effect rating.
quote: Analogical inference appears to be mediated by building and then running a causal model.
limits: Full text is behind the APA paywall and could not be opened. This settles what the paper claims, not the numbers.
agent_relevance: Confirms that an overlap score is a poor stand-in for trust in one specific inference; an O7 check should ask whether a causal background factor (a preventer) is shared.

source: Day & Gentner (2007) Nonintentional analogical inference in text comprehension. Memory & Cognition 35(1), 39-49
finding: Readers used information from an earlier, relationally similar passage to interpret a later one, reported no awareness of doing so, and the effect depended on the structural mapping (not mere priming). Reading-speed data suggest the inference happened during encoding of the target and not only at the later test.
numbers: Abstract only (Europe PMC). The Northwestern PDF is a scanned image with no text layer and no OCR tool was available, so no cell values were read.
quote: analogical mapping ... can sometimes operate without intent or even awareness.
limits: Abstract only. Human reading, not LLMs.
agent_relevance: Humans make analogical inferences without being asked. By analogy an LLM with a relevant source in context may do the same (see d15), so O7 should run whenever a source is present. That step is an inference, not a measured result.

source: Holyoak, Lee & Lu (2010) Analogical and category-based inference: a theoretical integration with Bayesian causal models. J Exp Psychol: General
finding: A Bayesian causal-model theory, with no free parameters in the cases tested, predicts people's probability judgements about causal predictions made from source knowledge about generative and preventive causes. It says analogical inferences are partly separate from overall mapping quality.
numbers: Abstract only (Europe PMC); no data read.
quote: analogical inferences are partially dissociable from overall mapping quality
limits: Same group as Lee and Holyoak 2008, so not an independent replication of Gentner or Markman; abstract only.
agent_relevance: A second, probabilistic formulation of the same caution: score each projected fact by its causal support, not by whole-mapping similarity.

source: Lassaline (1996) Structural alignment in induction and similarity. J Exp Psychol: Learning, Memory, and Cognition 22(3), 754-770
finding: Across five experiments with novel and familiar animals, shared attributes raised both similarity and inductive strength. Shared causal relations raised similarity, but binding causal relations that connect a shared attribute to the candidate inference raised inductive strength. This is a candidate-inference result from a paper outside the Clement-Gentner and Markman set.
numbers: Abstract only (Europe PMC); no sample sizes or cell means read.
quote: binding causal relations ... were important for inductive strength
limits: Author affiliation not checked, so independence from Gentner's lab is not confirmed. Animals and attributes; participants presumably students. Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Gives a possibly independent source for the grounding rule: a projected fact needs a causal link to a shared fact. Gap 9 is only weakly addressed.

source: Webb, Holyoak & Lu (2024) Evidence from counterfactual tasks supports emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Reply to Hodel and West and to Lewis and Mitchell. The authors say the critics misread their materials and report that models also generalise to counterfactual (permuted-alphabet) variants. The dispute over letter-string transfer is therefore still open between the labs.
numbers: Abstract page only; no numbers read.
limits: Abstract only; written by the original claim's team. Pre-reasoning models (GPT-3 to GPT-4).
agent_relevance: K09 and K10 carry a live dispute, so do not use the letter-string failure alone to justify a code check.
